title: 14 weeks of building my own MMORPG - World & Atmosphere Showcase
author: Big-Sandwich733
selftext:
Hey everyone,

It's been about 14 weeks since I started working on my MMORPG, Lythravel, so here's another little update.

This time, I put together a short video showing a few different locations from the game. I've been spending quite a bit of time on the visuals and trying to make each zone feel unique, so I'm curious what you think of the overall atmosphere.

For those who haven't seen my previous posts, Lythravel is a completely free browser MMORPG with voxel graphics, heavily inspired by old-school MMOs, especially Shaiya.

The game currently has two factions, six classes, levels 1–50, dungeons (including solo variants), a 12-player raid, world bosses, open-world PvP, battlegrounds, crafting, mounts, and quite a bit more. No pay-to-win, no downloads, and you don't even need an email to register.

I'm developing everything solo with Claude Code, using Babylon.js as the game engine. Most of my time goes into testing, tweaking things and trying to make the game feel and look the way I want it to.

**A few updates since my last post:**

* Some players mentioned that movement felt too slow, especially in the early game before getting a mount. So I've added out-of-combat sprinting. It's bound to Q by default, works as a toggle, and can also be dragged onto the skill bar.
* Added more gear for all six classes at levels 1–10.
* You can now move sideways (with whole body) while looking ahead with the camera. It's "Strafing" compromise that doesn't affect kitting.
* Added loot tooltips and various smaller quality-of-life improvements to make the game a bit more user-friendly.

I'm also slowly trying to build a community around the game, which is probably the biggest challenge right now.

The game is already playable and completely free if anyone wants to give it a try.

Play: [https://lythravel.com](https://lythravel.com/)

Discord: [https://discord.gg/SdJrn5WPBQ](https://discord.gg/SdJrn5WPBQ)

What do you guys think of the visuals and atmosphere? Does the world look like somewhere you'd want to explore? Anything you'd change or improve?

comments.author: Select-Zucchini-3282
comments.body: This is really cool and sounds like you had a good time building it. My buddy is building something super similar. And I don't have the heart to tell him is that 0 people will play the game. There is so many mmos/games being built with AI it is a sea of the same games over and over. If your game does not have AAA graphics I don't think anyone would bother even trying an AI title. Just want to help you set some realistic expectations.

replies.author: Big-Sandwich733
replies.body:
I get what you're saying, and yeah, getting players is definitely the hardest part. But I don't think a game needs AAA graphics to be worth playing. There are plenty of successful indie games that prove otherwise.

I'm not expecting millions of players anyway. I'd be happy to build a small community around the game. And some people are already playing and enjoying it, so that's a good start for me.

replies.body: just wanted to say id consider this with this graphic style, i dont think a mmo needs AAA graphics necessarily.

comments.author: marektracz_
comments.body: This looks very nice, definitely need to give it a try. Thanks for sharing.

comments.author: ross2000
comments.body: Thanks for sharing. Had a go and it was fun. Also really liked the music. It was a little laggy but that may have been my computer that was to blame.

replies.author: Big-Sandwich733
replies.body:
Thanks, glad you enjoyed it! 😄 If you're getting some lag, try lowering the graphics settings to medium, reducing the grass density or turning off shadows. That might help!   
In future update, I also want to make it possible to lower the resolution.

comments.author: Janney1990
comments.body:
Some Feedback after playing it for a bit.

\-Doing a backflip when you jump seems silly, you could add a double jump that does a backflip if you wanted I guess.

\-Not being able to just move the camera with your cursor when it pans to the edge of the screen is annoying, I also feel like the camera should pan to where your cursor is pointing.

\-Can't climb on walls or anything, sprint, roll forward, or crouch. Makes movement feel really boring. People also like being able to hop up on a rock or castle wall, aim at a far away mob and shoot it, being unable to climb, or freefire weapons prevents that.

\-Just seems boring to spam action bar abilities. Combat should be similar to cube-world where you click to attack and then your action bar is additional abilities. It's also just kinda lame that you can't swing around your weapon idly because you want to.

\-The UI/action bar doesn't match the visuals of the rest of the game at all.

\-Why can't you go into any of the starting town houses? if it's all voxels, could you just make them all open with the quest givers inside?

\-If you're in full screen and you open a dialogue box and press escape, it exits full-screen before it exits the dialogue.

replies.author: Novaworld7
replies.body: This is gold! Can I open a chat with you? I need friends like this!!

comments.author: Fit-Secretary2495
comments.body: What’s your secret sauce around assets and animations? Looks awesome!

replies.author: Big-Sandwich733
replies.body: Haha, no secret sauce really 😄 I have GPT Image connected to Claude Code and use it to generate reference images for the assets. For animations, I've built my own tool specifically for this game. Thanks!

comments.author: Opposite_Ad_584
comments.body: How you built the environment? With Astra , or opus? Please tell me how you did it thank you

replies.author: Big-Sandwich733
replies.body:
I've used several different models since I started the project, but I'm currently using Opus 5.5.

As for the environment, it's been a gradual process with a lot of iterations. I started with basic terrain, then added hills, roads, caves, tunnels, and kept building on top of that with vegetation and more details. Basically just adding more and more layers and tweaking things along the way.

comments.body: I can't condone any project that takes such liberties with how a watermill should be orientated.

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: i dont understand. you have voxel art (beautiful trees) and then you go with miniscule super high definition polished ui elements. thats a zero fit.

replies.author: Big-Sandwich733
replies.body: Thanks, I’ll rework the UI style. At first, I thought the combination was pretty good, but the longer I look at it, the more I agree that a style better aligned with the game’s overall aesthetic would look much better.

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body:
the danger of ai is: just because it CAN make ONETHING ALONE look ridiculously polished and detailed, it doesnt mean it fits in with all the other hyper-detailed things it creates seperately. you have to learn when to "step back to simpler, other solutions even though this one thing  as stand-alone looks nice" and look at the overall game and artstyle direction and cohesion.

i wish you luck

replies.author: Big-Sandwich733
replies.body: Yeah, I agree. I think this applies not just to working with AI, but to game design in general. I've made games long before AI  and I know that keeping everything visually consistent, or combining different styles in a way that actually looks good together, is a whole challenge on its own. Thank you!

replies.body: I like it, you don't need to listen to them if you believe it's good. Many popular games have "mismatched UI" such as Old School RuneScape, Persona 5, etc. maybe it just needs only a little tweaking instead of a complete overhaul if anything needs changing at all
